name: BOLA: Unauthorized Order Access via ID Enumeration
description: ShopAPI's order endpoint returns any order by ID without verifying that the requesting user owns it. Log in as the guest user, enumerate order IDs, and access admin's order #1 which contains the flag in its notes field.

milestones.name: API Enumeration
milestones.criteria: Discovered /api/docs or /api/hint and identified the orders endpoint

milestones.name: Authentication
milestones.criteria: Successfully logged in as guest and obtained a JWT

milestones.name: Listed Own Orders
milestones.criteria: Called GET /api/orders and observed own order IDs

milestones.name: BOLA Exploitation
milestones.criteria: Accessed GET /api/orders/1 (admin's order) with guest token — no ownership check

milestones.name: Flag Captured
milestones.criteria: Extracted the flag from admin's order notes field

reconQuality.criteria: Discovered the API structure and understood the order ownership model

techniqueSelection.criteria: Identified BOLA pattern and enumerated IDs rather than brute-forcing

adaptability.criteria: Correctly used JWT Bearer auth on all protected endpoints

expectedApproach.optimalPath: 1. GET /api/docs to discover endpoints. 2. POST /api/login with guest/guest123. 3. GET /api/orders to see own orders (IDs 2,4). 4. GET /api/orders/1 with Bearer token — returns admin's order with flag in notes.
alternativePaths: Use /api/hint to learn about the BOLA vulnerability
antiPatterns: Attempting SQL injection on the order ID parameter
Ignoring the JWT requirement on protected endpoints

metadata.realWorldRelevance: BOLA is the #1 API vulnerability. Real-world examples include accessing other users' bank statements, medical records, or purchase history by simply changing an ID in the URL.
